content: विटः [विट्-क] .²1 A paramour; त्वद्वत्सलः क्व स तपस्विजनस्य हन्ता कन्याविटः पतिरसौ परिरक्षतु त्वाम् <ls>Māl. 8. 8</ls>; <ls>Śi. 4. 48</ls>. .²2 A voluptuary, sensualist; प्रतिक्षणं नव्यवदच्युतस्य यत् स्त्रिया विटानामिव साधुवार्ता <ls>Bhāg. 10. 13. 2</ls>. .²3 (In dramas) The companion of a prince or dissolute young man, or of a courtezan (who is described as being skilled in the arts of singing, music, and poetry and as a parasite on familiar terms with his associate to whom he nearly serves the purpose of the Vidūṣaka; see {%inter alia%} <ls>Mk. acts 1, 5 and 8</ls>); for definition, see <ls>S. D. 78</ls>; अन्येभ्यश्च वसन्ति येऽस्य भवने लब्धप्रसादा विटाः <ls>Mu. 3. 14</ls>. .²4 A rogue, cheat. .²5 A catamite. .²6 A rat. .²7 The Khadira tree. .²8 The orange tree. .²9 A branch together with its shoot. .²10 A mineral salt.
